protocol: Selection criteria were fixed from the solver's DOCUMENTED limits before any instance was downloaded or run, and this file was written before the first solve. Compatibility screening (does the file parse?) is performed after freezing and is not a performance observation; an instance that turns out incompatible is recorded as such and NOT replaced.

a_priori_criteria.constraints_rationale: the dual simplex maintains a DENSE m x m basis inverse allocated up front (8*m^2 bytes) and branch-and-cut solves every node with it; this is the documented dispatcher ceiling, not a tuning choice
a_priori_criteria.excluded_tags_rationale: the MPS reader rejects INDICATORS and SOS sections outright rather than silently dropping them, so such instances cannot be represented

difficulty_caveat: MIPLIB's easy/hard/open status describes REFERENCE solvers, not ours. It was not used to select for tractability and carries no expectation that our engine finds these easy.

selection.name: flugpl
selection.reference_kind_basis: MIPLIB status 'easy'/'hard' means the instance has been solved to proven optimality by reference solvers; 'open' means the value is a best-known incumbent with no optimality proof
selection.structural_rationale: general integers WITH continuous variables; aggregations / variable_bound structure; smallest mixed general-integer case in the compatible pool

selection.reference_kind_basis: MIPLIB status 'easy'/'hard' means the instance has been solved to proven optimality by reference solvers; 'open' means the value is a best-known incumbent with no optimality proof
selection.structural_rationale: PURE general integer (no binaries, no continuous) -- exercises branching on non-binary domains
